AppSettingsDTO.title: AppSettingsDTO
AppSettingsDTO.description:
Organizer view of AppSettings at GET /settings.

Flat, with the same field names `UpdateAppSettingsInput` takes, so what the
page reads it can send back as is.

award_id.title: Award Id
award_id.description: UUIDv7 the client generates once per award form.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.description: ALTCHA challenge, passed verbatim to the widget; its fields are the provider's, not part of this API. Null when captcha is disabled.

ImportScheduleForm.title: ImportScheduleForm
ImportScheduleForm.description:
Multipart body of POST /schedule/import, named so the spec and the
generated client don't carry FastAPI's ``Body_import_schedule``.

InvalidScheduleFileProblem.title: InvalidScheduleFileProblem
InvalidScheduleFileProblem.description:
ProblemDetails narrowed to INVALID_SCHEDULE_FILE, for the import route's docs.

Gives the frontend a typed `reason` union to check its copy against, as the
code enum does for codes. The response itself is still built from the
exception's details dict; a unit test keeps the two in step.

InvalidScheduleFileReason.title: InvalidScheduleFileReason
InvalidScheduleFileReason.description:
Why a schedule spreadsheet was rejected.

Travels to the client inside the error `details`, so each member is part of
the API contract — the frontend switches on it to pick Russian copy.

OAuthProvidersOutput.title: OAuthProvidersOutput
OAuthProvidersOutput.description:
The social login providers the login screen should offer, in order.

Only the provider ids: labels, icons and brand colours are the frontend's to
own. This is deployment config, not a fixed set — a provider may be built in
yet withheld here because it is unreachable from this host.

ProblemDetails.title: ProblemDetails
ProblemDetails.description:
An RFC 9457 problem details object; every error response is one.

`code` is our extension member and what the client branches on: a closed
set, stamped into the spec as an enum. `type` is derived from it, so the two
never disagree. Problem-specific members (`retry_after`, `reason`, `errors`,
…) sit beside these at the top level, as RFC 9457 §3.2 extensions do.

PublicConfigDTO.title: PublicConfigDTO
PublicConfigDTO.description:
Public, unauthenticated projection of AppSettings served at GET /config.

Deliberately omits `limits` (ADR-0008 projection tuning is organizer-only).
Carries the raw `festival_start` and `festival_end` so the client can run the
live countdown and pick its before/during/after phase itself — flipping at
each boundary without provoking a 403 on a guarded endpoint. Voting
availability is intentionally not here: the UI reads it per-user from
GET /voting/status (which already reflects the time range as a DISABLED
state), so a second public copy would only be a redundant source of truth to
drift.

ScheduleChangeType.title: ScheduleChangeType
ScheduleChangeType.description:
How to read a `ScheduleChange`'s `changed_event_id`/`related_entry_id`.

SET_AS_CURRENT: `changed_event_id` is the new current event (None if the
    current event was unchecked); `related_entry_id` is the event that was
    current before this change.
MOVED: `related_entry_id` is the entry `changed_event_id` sat right after
    before the move — a block start when the event opened its block. To
    undo, place `changed_event_id` back after `related_entry_id` — or at
    the top of the order if `related_entry_id` is None.
SKIPPED / UNSKIPPED: `related_entry_id` is unused.

ScheduleEntryType.title: ScheduleEntryType
ScheduleEntryType.description:
What a row of the programme is.

EVENT: something that happens on stage — an act, a break, the opening.
BLOCK_START: the heading of a programme block. Every entry after it, up to
    the next block start, belongs to that block, so moving an event across
    a block start moves it into the other block.

mailing_id.title: Mailing Id
mailing_id.description: UUIDv7 the client generates once per broadcast form.

SocialProvider.title: SocialProvider
SocialProvider.description:
External identity providers the app accepts.

Doubles as the `iss` stand-in when matching an identity: there is exactly one
issuer per member, so `(provider, subject)` is the `(iss, sub)` pair OpenID
Connect asks relying parties to key on. Adding a member means adding an
Authlib client in `main/ioc/auth.py`, its **own** callback URI (RFC 9700
§4.4.2.2 — see the module docstring in `presentation/web/oauth.py`), a
hand-written migration for the CHECK constraint backing the column, an entry
in the frontend's `PROVIDER_META` (its login button), and — to actually offer
it — its name in `WEB__ENABLED_OAUTH_PROVIDERS` (`WebConfig`), the deployment
gate the login screen reads via `/auth/oauth/providers`.

SyncRunDTO.title: SyncRunDTO
SyncRunDTO.description:
A sync run as shown to an organizer.

Deliberately omits ``by_user_id``: the row records who triggered the run for
the audit trail, but the page only answers "is the data fresh, and did the
last run succeed?", which status and timestamps already cover. Keeping the
actor off the wire avoids a users join and any handling of the system user
id on the frontend.

SyncSource.title: SyncSource
SyncSource.description:
External system a sync run pulls from.

The value doubles as the URL path segment (``POST /sync/{source}``) and the
stored column value, so it is part of both the API and the DB contract.

place_after_entry_id.title: Place After Entry Id
place_after_entry_id.description: Entry to place the event after. Null moves it to the top.

UpdateScheduleEventBody.title: UpdateScheduleEventBody
UpdateScheduleEventBody.description: One change per request: each is its own announcement and undo step.

UserRefDTO.title: UserRefDTO
UserRefDTO.description:
A person attached to a record, in the field named for their role there
(`user`, `awarded_by`, `created_by`, …); null when nobody is (a system
action, a deleted account).

SSEEventName.description:
Canonical names for every Server-Sent Event the backend emits.

Published in the OpenAPI spec as the `GET /events` item's `event` type, so
the generated `SseEventName` union checks the frontend's `SSEEventMap`.

Naming standard (see docs/backend.md "Realtime (SSE)"):
  * snake_case, single token — NO dots. The NATS subject is built as
    `sse.broadcast.{event_name}` / `sse.user.{user_id}.{event_name}` and
    consumers subscribe with a single-token wildcard (`sse.broadcast.*`).
    A dot in the name would split into extra subject tokens and silently
    stop matching that wildcard.
  * Prefer `<entity>_<event>` for new names.
